directChecks.method: Intersect x=-25.638 with the 45-degree segment from (-29.167,23.108) to (-24.525,27.75): y=x+52.275. Both intersection parameters lie inside both spans.

directChecks.sourceInterpretation: pd-input.tsx passive array maps a to pin1 and b to pin2. R_PD_ALERT pin1=V3V3, pin2=PD_ALERT; R_INPUT_FAULT pin1=V3V3, pin2=INPUT_FAULT_N. Source_net_1, source_net_21 and source_net_23 remain separate roots.

strengths: All declared named nets remain distinct under independent source-trace unioning; no net-key ambiguities conceal foreign-net contacts.
Every actual via and copper pour resolves to an explicit source net or a trace net, and all actual trace anchors agree after resolving manual-via terminal aliases.
The photographed same-layer crossing is electrically legal V3V3 copper on both traces; resistor pin2 alert/fault signal sides stay on distinct named nets.

findings.explanation: The name ALERT_INNER2_TRUNK suggests an alert signal even though the copper is a V3V3 supply link feeding pull-up resistor pin1 sides. This materially confuses visual short-circuit review.

353 manual-via source-terminal aliases are not joined by a direct source_trace; their correct net must be recovered from the explicit pcb_via barrel owner. Also 89 connectsTo entries reference source traces rather than PCB ports. These are resolvable conventions, not copper shorts, but a simpler checker can misclassify them or miss ownership.
evidence: Example: pcb_via_272 explicitly source_net_4 and connectivity net95; source_port_1261 top belongs to source_manually_placed_via_272 and has no direct source key.

findings.explanation: The two V3V3 paths intersect before independently reaching the same R_INPUT_FAULT supply side through separate vias. A single deliberate supply branch could be easier to inspect. The existing contact is permitted and no reroute is required for isolation.
evidence: pcb_trace_193 and pcb_trace_246 intersect on inner2

suspectedShortAssessment.verdict: The pictured crossing is an intentional or harmless same-net V3V3 junction, not a foreign-net short.
suspectedShortAssessment.scope: This resolves source ownership at the pictured junction. It does not assert whole-board geometric clearance or finished-Gerber equivalence.

topImprovements: Rename ALERT_INNER2_TRUNK and its launches to expose V3V3 supply ownership.
Represent manual-via terminal net membership explicitly and normalize trace endpoint references so simple netlist audits do not depend on special resolver conventions.
Consider consolidating the pictured redundant V3V3 branch if the broader routing review shows a shorter simpler option without degrading clearance or supply feed geometry.
limitations: Independently checked logical isolation and metadata consistency, not a complete geometric foreign-net overlap scan. Other geometry reviewers must evaluate pad/trace/via/pour contact and clearances.
No fabricated-board, Gerber, soldermask, manufacturing, power-up, or dynamic fault-behavior acceptance is inferred.
Score is for static net ownership and isolation auditability; complete routing economy and power-current suitability require other assigned reviews.
